主要内容: President Donald Trump signed the GOP tax bill into law on Friday, marking the culmination of a months-long effort to pass the legislation through the Republican-controlled Congress. At the same event, Trump signed an emergency funding bill to keep the federal government open through January 19. The $1.5 trillion tax bill includes significant corporate tax cuts, which Trump claimed have caused "corporations to literally go wild." The tax plan also includes a short-term spending bill to fund the government, avoiding a potential partial shutdown. The GOP argues the tax cuts will boost business investment and hiring, while Democrats criticize the plan as a giveaway to corporations at the expense of the middle class. The short-term spending bill, while less contentious, included a "pay-go waiver" to suspend rules on funding certain programs. The enactment of the tax bill is seen as a major victory for Republicans ahead of the 2018 midterm elections.
